title: Create and apply Drizzle migration
description: Generate the initial Drizzle migration from the schema definitions and apply it to create the SQLite database file with all tables. Also ensure the database is initialized on app startup.
acceptanceCriteria: `./drizzle/` directory contains at least one migration SQL file
Running `npm run db:migrate` creates `./data/prospectforge.db` with all five tables
Database file contains: batches, prospects, media, sent_emails, settings tables
All table columns match the schema definitions
Migration runs without errors on a fresh machine (data directory is created if missing)

steps.details: Run `npx drizzle-kit generate`. This reads `src/db/schema.ts` and produces SQL migration files in `./drizzle/`. Inspect the generated SQL to confirm all CREATE TABLE statements are present.

steps.description: Update src/db/migrate.ts to create data directory if missing
steps.details: Update `src/db/migrate.ts` to include `fs.mkdirSync('./data', { recursive: true })` before instantiating the database. This ensures the migration works on a fresh clone.

steps.description: Run the migration and verify the database
steps.details: Run `npm run db:migrate`. Then open the SQLite file with `sqlite3 ./data/prospectforge.db` or a GUI tool. Run `.tables` to verify all five tables exist. Run `.schema prospects` to verify all columns are present.

In `src/db/index.ts`, after creating the db instance, call migrate synchronously so the database is always up-to-date when the Next.js app starts. Import `migrate` from `drizzle-orm/better-sqlite3/migrator` and call `migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: './drizzle' })` before exporting `db`.

technicalNotes: Drizzle migrations are additive — running them on an already-migrated database is safe (it tracks applied migrations in a `__drizzle_migrations` table).
Add `drizzle/` to version control so migrations are tracked.
Add `./data/` to .gitignore so the database file itself is not committed.
